newsitem.title: UK: India sees growing natural rubber deficit.
newsitem.headline: India sees growing natural rubber deficit.

text.p: India, a key natural rubber producer, is likely to raise synthetic rubber use to meet the country's growing rubber demand and help plug a shortfall in domestic natural rubber output, officials said.
India's Rubber Board chairman K.J. Mathew said in an interview that India's rubber consumption pattern would gradually change in favour of the oil- and chemical-based synthetic rubber.
India uses natural rubber and synthetic rubber in the proportion of 80:20. Mathew said the ratio could change to 70:30, still in favour of natural rubber.
Mathew was speaking at the start of a two-day International Rubber Forum, which is attended by more than 140 industry and trade officials from more than 20 countries.
He said India could face a natural rubber supply deficit of 29,000 tonnes in 1997. The deficit could grow to nearly 100,000 in 2000 and 300,000 in 2010.
The country produced 540,000 tonnes of natural rubber and 62,000 tonnes of synthetic rubber in 1996.
Consumption reached 700,000 tonnes in 1996 and demand is expected to outpace supply for the next 10 years, Mathew said.
The demand for tyres and tubes in the nation of more than 900 million people is growing by a hefty 10 percent a year.
Western industry executives say India and China offer the best growth prospects for tyre and rubber goods demand by the turn of the century.
